Pour upon me your wisdom, understanding, and knowledge (Liqutei Tefilot I:58 part 1) by Reb Noson Sternhartz of Nemyriv (ca. 1820s) and "A Student's Prayer" as adapted by Rabbi Morrison David Bial (1962)

tei:div.tei:head: Pour upon me your wisdom, understanding, and knowledge (Liqutei Tefilot I:58 part 1) by Reb Noson Sternhartz of Nemyriv (ca. 1820s) and "A Student's Prayer" as adapted by Rabbi Morrison David Bial (1962)

tei:lg.tei:l: May I learn Thy Torah of loving-kindness,
And may I learn that holiness means
bringing love to friends and fellow students,
May I in reverence of Thee
Keep far from sin and wrongdoing.
That I may be a vehicle of grace and loving-kindness.
Guide my tongue when I speak with my fellows
That my words may be filled with grace and beauty,
That my actions may be of goodness and help.
Before Thee and before my fellow man.
